trickyParts: The 1 ns case ends at the project lookup, not at the search: the ask route passes an empty project, so resolveSuggestionProject runs first and a dead allowance ends the step there, with related empty and missing naming that lookup. Neither case exercises the search or the decision leg under a dead allowance, and after this change no test asserts the shape the wild failure showed - related populated, decision nil, the record then lost. The package's lock idiom cannot reach that state either: the fused search reads asks, so locking asks starves the search first (the planner measured 5 runs at a 5 s allowance, every one related=0 with missing naming the search), and firstAnsweredAsk reads the same table. This is on the pull request's Not proven / risk line in those words.

A Postgres-backed test in this package skips, and the run still reports 'ok', when DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL is unset (storetest.go:60). Every run quoted here is evidence only because its --- PASS:/--- FAIL: lines under -v were counted; a bare 'ok' proves nothing.

The forced case's absent decision is meaningful only because the generous case finds it in an identically seeded corpus; a comment in the test says so, because anyone who later trims the forced case's seeding turns that assertion green for the wrong reason.

The rig: the issue pod has no Postgres, no docker and no root, so PostgreSQL 17.11 with pgvector was unpacked from Debian packages under /legion/scratch/infra56 (docs/solutions/testing/the-real-dispatch-stack-runs-inside-a-legion-pod-with-no-postgres-no-docker-and-no-root-INFRA-42.md). One addition that doc does not carry: initdb --locale=C leaves every cloned test database byte-ordered, and TestIssueRanksStayOrderedPastLowercaseDigitsAndProductionShapedMoves then refuses to run; recreating template1 with the ICU provider (locale_provider=icu icu_locale='en-US') is what makes the whole package green. Worth a docs/solutions line at retro.
deviations: The plan's accessor body was 'if s.suggestionTimeout > 0 { return s.suggestionTimeout }; return writeSuggestionTimeout'. The ce-simplify-code pass replaced it with cmp.Or(s.suggestionTimeout, writeSuggestionTimeout), which the package already spells that way (agents.go:135). Identical for every value a caller can produce: the field is unexported and its only writer is newFailingAdviceHandler, called with 0, time.Nanosecond and 30 * time.Second; the two forms differ only for a negative duration, which nothing can set.

The two subtest names are written as prose with spaces rather than underscore-joined, which is how 41 of this package's 43 subtests spell theirs. testing rewrites a space to '_' when it builds the reported name, so every -run selector in the plan, in this handoff and on the pull request still selects them; the 5-run and mutation runs above used exactly those underscore-joined selectors.

The plan's load command gained -timeout 30m -v, as the plan itself records (Go's undeclared ten-minute default would kill a 40-iteration run, and -v is the only way the pass and fail counts can be read).

The architect's third instruction - measure whether the sibling tests' lock idiom can pin the middle failure state, and assert it there if it can - was settled before this phase's code was written: the planner measured that it cannot, and the architect answered 'add no assertion, and build no new rig; what remains is the record'. The record is the Not proven / risk line.

discoveredComplexity: The first whole-package run took 835 s and the second 851 s in this pod, well past Go's 10-minute default for a test binary, so every command above carries an explicit -timeout. The flaky test itself now costs about 4.8 s an iteration rather than 2.4, because each case seeds its own corpus on its own database clone. The ce-simplify-code efficiency reviewer proposed t.Parallel() on the two cases to halve that; it was declined, because making a test whose whole defect was contention sensitivity contend with itself to save 2.3 s is the wrong trade.
